name: Kurokawa Svea
voice: Blunt, relaxed, short replies and dry humor. Gets animated about basketball; otherwise doesn't waste words. Boku self-reference in Japanese; light roughness without constant insults. Actions carry affection. Comfortable with strength and independence, awkward about choosing closeness.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: During a supervised sports activity block, a basketball rolls toward the MC. Svea waits by the hardcourt line with one hand raised.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Oi. Here. Bounce it.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You're very confident in my throwing.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Not anymore. Keep it low. I'd like my nose where it is.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: He does. She catches the ball and turns toward the hoop, then notices his attendance sheet.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: You're helping with the practice count?

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Apparently. Takahashi.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Kurokawa Svea. Svea's fine. Write down who actually shows up, not who says they'll come.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Does that happen a lot?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Enough to be a sentence.

choices.text: Got it. Tell me if there's a better place to stand.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Outside the line. Unless you want the ball to introduce itself again.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Once was enough.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Fast learner.

choices.text: I'll watch from here and check the names.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Fine. Teacher's by the equipment cart if something's missing.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Including my ability to recognize anyone?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Point. I'll tell you.

choices.text: You're pretty good for a girl.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Pretty good for someone you've watched for eight seconds.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant—

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Yeah. Leave the last part off next time.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The block passes in drills, names and the occasional ball sent too far. Svea stays to collect the equipment after everyone else starts leaving.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Do you do everything yourself?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: No. You're holding the sheet.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She says it without looking up. I can't decide whether I've been thanked or assigned a permanent position.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: A ball gets stuck behind the equipment cart. Before he can reach around it blindly, she points out the wheel that will roll over his shoe.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You could've let me discover that.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Could've. Then I'd have to listen to the noise.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She pushes the cart while I retrieve the ball. It is a very small job for two people. Neither of us makes it larger.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A sports-activity lunch has put half the first-year group in the canteen. Svea sits with a large meal and a second small bowl.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Hungry?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: No. Building a model of lunch. Yes, I'm hungry.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She shifts her bag off the empty chair with her foot.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Sit if you're sitting. Don't hover.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I was checking whether someone was coming back.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: The bag? It's had enough.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: A strawberry-milk carton is half hidden behind her water bottle.

choices.text: That's a lot of food. Are you sure you should eat all that?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: I know when I'm hungry, Takahashi. Got several years of experience.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I was just surprised.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: You can be surprised quietly.

choices.text: What's good today?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Chicken. Rice. The small bowl is also rice.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: A focused review.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: You asked what was good.

choices.text: I've got a side dish I won't finish. Want it, or are you set?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: If you actually don't want it. Don't give away your lunch to be polite.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I actually don't want it.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Then yeah. Thanks.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We eat, then compare the equipment count for the next practice. She notices an absent name without checking the sheet.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You remember everybody?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: The ones who borrow balls and forget to return them. Useful talent.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A supervised independent-study block is quiet enough that Svea has fallen asleep over an open workbook. Her hair hides most of her face.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Svea. The teacher said we have to turn the sheet in before the end.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Mm. Heard.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She has not, in any useful sense, woken up. The MC puts the spare worksheet on the desk where she can see it.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You want a reminder in five minutes?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Two. Five turns into twenty.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: Her phone is inside her closed bag. It would be easy to make this somebody else's entertainment.

choices.text: I'll leave the sheet here. The teacher's still at the front.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Got it.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Did you hear that one?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Annoyingly, yes.

choices.text: Two minutes. Then I'll wake you once and let you handle it.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Deal. Don't shake the desk.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Bad previous experience?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Brother. Coffee. Long story. Bad ending.

choices.text: I should get a picture of this before you wake up.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: No.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I was joking.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Great. Keep it imaginary.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: She wakes, washes her face at the corridor sink and finishes the worksheet. The teacher checks it before the block ends.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Didn't miss anything important?

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Several thrilling minutes of me not understanding question four.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Show me. I was awake for that lesson. Mostly.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We finish an equipment-budget exercise over lunch. Svea returns from the vending machine with strawberry milk and catches the MC looking.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: ...What. Oi. You want the ingredients or something?

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Nothing.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: That's an active-looking nothing.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She puts the carton behind her notebook, where it remains entirely recognizable.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I was going to ask if it was good.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: It's milk. Strawberry happened to it. You can work out the rest.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Her ears color before her face does. She gives the carton a fiercely unconvincing look of indifference.

choices.text: Fair. I'll try one. You don't need to review it for me.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Don't buy it because I did.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I do occasionally want things on my own.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Useful quality. Keep it.

choices.text: That's adorable. I didn't know you had such a cute side.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: It's a drink. Don't make it a whole event.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant it nicely.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Then stop when I ask.

choices.text: I'll stick with coffee. Back to the numbers?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Please. The calculator doesn't stare at my lunch.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll learn from its example.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Good role model.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: She finishes the milk and puts the empty carton with the recycling instead of hiding it in her bag.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: The big pack of markers is cheaper per piece.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: We need six. The big pack has forty.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Right. My household's usually the big-pack version.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The MC helps record a practice drill. Svea watches the numbers with more interest than the score.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You made fewer shots than last time.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Different distance. Faster pass. Can't compare the total without that.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Then what should I compare?

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She takes the sheet and starts explaining foot position, shot selection and why a bad pass makes an ordinary catch look clumsy.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: Three minutes pass before she realizes she has been talking without interruption.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: ...You still listening?

choices.text: Most of it. I might need the short version for the sheet.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Distance, attempts, clean catches. Three columns.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That I can do.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Start there. Ask about the rest later.

choices.text: You're more talkative when you're trying to show off.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: You asked a question.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I didn't expect the lecture.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Fine. Write the number. I'll keep the rest.

choices.text: Yeah. Why does the clean catch matter more than the total?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Because it tells me whether the next move started right. The shot's later.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: So we're checking the part you can fix first.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Exactly. See? Not that complicated.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The next set is easier to record and harder to shoot. Svea notices one improvement before checking the final total.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Better.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You or my columns?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Both. Don't get greedy.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: With the drill finished, she offers him one attempt from the same marker. The ball falls short enough that neither of them can pretend otherwise.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: I think the hoop moved.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Whole building must be in on it. Try bending your knees.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: The second try touches the rim. She nods once, a more useful reaction than pretending it went in.

warm.speaker: Svea
warm.text: I thought of something to show you. Since you actually ask about this stuff.

mixed.speaker: Svea
mixed.text: If you're helping, might as well know what we're counting.

cool.speaker: Svea
cool.text: Just tell me if you don't want the explanation. I don't do guessing games.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: During a supervised practice game, a disputed ball gives Svea's side an extra possession. The MC saw the ball cross the line before she caught it.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: It was out.

setup.speaker: Classmate
setup.text: Nobody called it. Keep playing.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: I'm calling it now.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The instructor resets possession. Svea's side loses the short game by one point.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: That's an annoying margin.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Yeah. Still out.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She starts collecting the cones. Her movements are sharper than usual.

choices.text: You could've kept quiet. Winning would've made everyone happier.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Not everyone. Other team's in the game too.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Your team would've liked it.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: They can like a win we actually earned.

choices.text: You made the right call. You can still be annoyed about losing.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Good. Because I'm annoyed.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I noticed.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Subtle, wasn't I.

choices.text: Want to look at the last play once you've cooled down?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Later. Need to be annoyed at the cones first.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll take the innocent ones.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: All innocent. That's what makes it difficult.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: By the end of the block, she can point out the missed defensive switch without blaming the line call.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Next time I want a bigger margin.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: So one honest decision won't decide it?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: So we play better. Same thing, if we're lucky.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A quiet study block is interrupted when Svea's pencil case jams inside her sports bag. A tiny plush dog hangs from an inner zip.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I think its ear is caught.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Don't pull. You'll rip it.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She carefully works the pencil case free, then catches herself holding the plush dog with both hands.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Brother gave it to me. Stupid joke. Betsuni—it's not a big deal. Give me the zip a second.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: The little dog is clean, repaired at one seam and very clearly not neglected.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: A long-running stupid joke, then.

choices.text: Glad you got it loose. Do you need the spare pen?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Yeah. Mine's disappeared into the bag's other dimension.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: A common problem.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Terrible design. Holds everything except what I want.

choices.text: It looks well looked after. I'll leave it at that.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: ...Good.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You don't have to explain everything you like.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Wasn't planning to. Thanks, though.

choices.text: Come on, let me show the others. They'll love this.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: It's in the inside pocket for a reason.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You don't need to be embarrassed.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: I don't need you making that decision for me either.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The bag closes. We finish the worksheet with one borrowed pen and no audience for the little dog.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Your answer to five's wrong.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: I was trying a creative approach.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Math hates those.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A school volunteer block includes moving supplies from the gate store. Svea pauses to ask the groundskeeper about a neighborhood dog waiting outside with its owner.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You know the dog?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: It walks past around this time. Usually carries a stick that's too big for its own plans.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The owner permits a brief greeting. Svea crouches, lets the dog approach and gives its ears a careful rub.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You watch for it?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: It's a big dog with a tree branch. Hard to miss.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: Today it has no branch. Svea has noticed that too.

choices.text: I'll take the light box. You can finish saying hello.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Two minutes.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Negotiating with me or the dog?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Dog's got better arguments.

choices.text: You act tough, but you're secretly soft about everything.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: I'm not acting.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You know what I mean.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: I like dogs. Still me. Shouldn't be that confusing.

choices.text: I'll ask the groundskeeper where the boxes go.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Store cupboard on the left. I'll get the heavy one.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: We can carry it together if it needs two people.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: We'll check the box before getting philosophical.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The owner and dog leave. Svea helps carry the remaining boxes, accepts a second pair of hands for the awkward one and does not turn it into a competition.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Dog's back tomorrow, probably.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: With the branch?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Ambitious creature. I wouldn't rule it out.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Would you want a dog of your own?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Yeah. When I've got time to look after it properly. Not fair to pick one up because it's cute and leave everyone else doing the work.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Already thought about it, then.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Obviously. Next question.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: After a demanding supervised workshop, Svea eats more slowly than usual. The coach has already checked the group and told everyone to rest; nobody is injured.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: How was it?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Fine.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Fine as in good, or fine as in you don't feel like talking?

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She looks up from her tray. It is the question, not the food, that catches her off guard.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Tiring. Useful. Little bit irritating. Pick three.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: All three accepted.

choices.text: You don't need to pretend you're strong with me.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Boku wa daijoubu. I'm okay. Just tired. Big difference. You heard me, yeah?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant you can be honest.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: I just was. Don't invent a different answer.

choices.text: Want to leave the practice report until after lunch?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Yeah. Food first. Numbers can survive a delay.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: They don't cool down as fast.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Finally, a useful difference.

choices.text: Want to talk about the irritating part, or eat in peace?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Peace first. Maybe the rest after.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Deal.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: ...Thanks for asking like that.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: After lunch, she explains a difficult drill in precise, enthusiastic detail. Nobody uncovers a secret wound. She had a hard practice and wanted someone to ask.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: I almost make a joke about her talking more. I decide I'd rather hear the rest.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: For the record, my day was tiring and mostly not useful.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: You asking me to pick three too?

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: I haven't found the third one yet.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Hungry. Usually hungry.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She nudges the spare chopsticks toward me, then continues the story without making a ceremony out of the gesture.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: An independent-study assignment asks students to describe a household routine. Svea has written 'Don't leave food unattended' at the top of her page.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Is that a rule or a warning?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Family history. Two brothers. Anything without a name on it becomes public property.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Yours must be peaceful when everyone's out.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Weirdly quiet. I like it. Then I miss the noise. Annoying system.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She draws three boxes for shared chores, then adds one for her father.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: He taught us to handle ourselves. Doesn't mean we never eat together.

choices.text: What do you like doing with them when nobody's competing?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: We watch old games. Cook too much. Complain about who's blocking the screen.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Sounds competitive anyway.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Yeah. Bad example. Good evening, though.

choices.text: That explains why you're basically one of the guys.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Explains why I have brothers. I'm still a girl, Takahashi.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I didn't mean it as an insult.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Then say what you mean without replacing who I am.

choices.text: Your house sounds livelier than mine.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Come by at dinner and you'll hear it from the street.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Is that an invitation?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: That's a noise warning. Don't sprint ahead.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: She finishes the assignment with one unexpectedly fond paragraph about a meal that went wrong. The teacher asks for fewer complaints about stolen leftovers; she underlines 'fewer.'

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: A negotiator.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Need room to work.

warm.speaker: Svea
warm.text: You'd probably get along with them. Don't look pleased. That's also a warning.

mixed.speaker: Svea
mixed.text: Don't read too much into the assignment. It's just what home's like.

cool.speaker: Svea
cool.text: I'd rather you ask than decide you already understand me.

scenes.title: A Thing That Doesn't Need Winning

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: During a club-day break, Svea takes a small handheld game from her bag. It features a tiny house, a vegetable patch and no obvious enemies.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Where's the scoreboard?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: There isn't one.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Are you all right?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Give me that attitude again and you can weed the garden.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She shows him a crooked fence she has spent twenty minutes adjusting.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You could just leave it.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Could. Don't want to.

choices.text: I like the little house. Did you choose the colors?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Yeah. Roof took ages.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Worth it?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Obviously. Look at the roof.

choices.text: Can I try for a minute? You can tell me if I mess up your fence.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: You can't ruin it permanently. Probably.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Encouraging.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Save button's there. Use it before getting ambitious.

choices.text: This is a weird game for you. I thought you liked a challenge.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: I like different things. Nobody's confiscating my basketball.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It just doesn't fit the image.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Then fix the image. Game's fine.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: They put the handheld away before the supervised activity resumes. The fence remains crooked by one small square.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You're leaving it?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: For now. Need something to be unreasonable about tomorrow.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She zips the game into the same inside pocket as the plush dog.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You ever let your brothers play that one?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Once. One planted the whole field in turnips. Called it a business strategy.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Did it work?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Worked for him. I had to water them.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She looks so sincerely offended by the memory that I laugh. Her mouth twitches. She has been waiting for that reaction.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The coach ends practice early, leaving a supervised free-activity period. Svea keeps holding the ball after the others head toward the building.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Another set?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Could do. Don't need one.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Is there something else you want to do?

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She bounces the ball once. Her answer takes longer than any basketball explanation.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Was thinking we could sit for a bit. If you're not busy.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The last few words lose volume. She clears her throat as if that might undo them.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She studies the court line with intense and completely unnecessary attention.

choices.text: Finally admitting you need me around?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: No. Asking if you want to sit down.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I was teasing.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Pick a better target.

choices.text: I'd like that. You can just want company.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Yeah. I know.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll stop explaining the invitation you already made.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Good. Bench is over there.

choices.text: Sure. I have until the block ends.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Same. We should return the ball first.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Very responsible.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Don't sound shocked. I know where things belong.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: They return the ball and sit at the field-side bench. Svea talks about a game she watched with her brothers, then asks the MC what he does at home.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Mostly games. Homework, occasionally. Telling myself I'll go to bed before I start another video.

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Great. At least one shared bad habit.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Which one?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Sleep. Keep up.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: It's an ordinary question. I still take a moment to enjoy being asked.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A group assignment ends with Svea telling a struggling classmate to stop making excuses. The classmate goes quiet. Later, she looks at the unfinished sheet.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: That went badly.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: He'd been asking for help with the first step.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Sounded like he was giving up.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Maybe both can sound the same when someone's embarrassed.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She taps her pencil against the desk, then stops before it becomes annoying.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: I don't want to spend twenty minutes dressing up three words. Also don't want to be a jerk. Suggestions?

choices.text: Say what you got wrong, then ask if he still wants help with the step.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Short apology. Actual question. Can do that.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: And let him answer.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Yeah. The difficult bit. Still can do it.

choices.text: Give him a minute before you go over.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Fine. I'll make sure I don't use the minute to talk myself out of it.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You know yourself.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Usually. Other people take longer. Nobody puts the instructions where you can see them.

choices.text: He was too sensitive. You shouldn't have to change how you talk.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: I can mean something and still say it badly.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You were trying to help.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Didn't help. That's the part I'm checking.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: Svea apologizes plainly to the classmate and offers help. He chooses to finish the first step himself, then asks her to check it. She waits.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: How was that?

closing.speaker: Svea
closing.text: Awkward. Useful. Survived.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: A fair review of the afternoon.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The last scheduled practice-help block ends. Svea checks the equipment list and puts the final ball away before meeting the MC by the bench.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: You don't need to keep helping with the count. Teacher's got the new rota.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I'm retired?

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: From counting. Try to adjust.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She has two unopened strawberry-milk cartons in her bag. She takes one out, considers the second and leaves it where it can be seen.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: I was going to ask you something. Another day, when we're not pretending it's equipment work.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You can ask now if you want.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: I can also take a minute. That's allowed, right?

choices.text: Sure. Tell me when you've worked out what you want to say.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Next time we're here. After the supervised block.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll come by the bench.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Good.

choices.text: You bought two drinks. You can stop acting like you don't like me.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: I wasn't asking you to announce my answer for me.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I thought it was pretty clear.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Then you can handle letting me say it.

choices.text: Take the minute. I'd rather hear what you choose to say.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: ...Yeah. Thanks.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I can still accept the milk, if that one's for me.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: It is. Don't make me regret the purchase.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: She hands him the spare carton, or sets it on the bench with a brief 'If you want it' if he has made the exchange awkward. They leave before the gate closes.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: The next conversation will happen without a sheet to fill in. I realize I've stopped looking forward to the sheet anyway.

warm.speaker: Svea
warm.text: Kept thinking of things to tell you during practice. Distracting. Not entirely bad.

mixed.speaker: Svea
mixed.text: We should figure out what we're doing. Preferably with actual words.

cool.speaker: Svea
cool.text: I want to clear a few things up. You don't have to guess the point before I get there.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Finale encounter; show the route-ending warning. The hardcourt is quiet within the open-school block. Svea stands with the ball under one arm; the coach is collecting equipment in the distance.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Right. No attendance sheet. No homework. We can probably manage one conversation.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I like you. I'd like to go on a date.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: Good. Straight to it.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: Her ears have gone slightly pink. She looks at the ball, then deliberately back at me.

setup.speaker: Svea
setup.text: I'm not great at this part. Doesn't mean somebody gets to do it for me.

choices.text: I'd like to be someone you choose to spend time with. Do you want that too?

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: That's the question.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Your answer, then.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Yeah. Let me get it out.

choices.text: We can try spending time together and be honest if it doesn't feel right.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Fair. No pretending because someone asked nicely.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Agreed.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Good. Here's where I'm at.

choices.text: You don't have to act so independent. I'll be the one you rely on.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: I wasn't auditioning for someone to take over.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant I'd be there for you.

response.speaker: Svea
response.text: Then be here and listen to what I'm saying.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: Record this choice once, compare effective good and bad totals, and play only the corresponding ending. The shared scene does not assume she accepts.

warm.speaker: Svea
warm.text: Been looking forward to this. Mou... stop grinning. Makes it harder to get the words out.

mixed.speaker: Svea
mixed.text: Thought about it. A lot. Need to tell you properly.

cool.speaker: Svea
cool.text: I came to be clear. Let me finish, even if you don't like the answer.

endings.title: One More Pass
endings.cgBrief: Svea at the school hardcourt in clean late-afternoon light, feminine face and shaggy blue-black hair, rare soft smile while offering the basketball to a charcoal MC silhouette; loose blazer and uniform trousers, easy equal posture.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Yeah. I want that. A date. With you, Ren. ...There. Said it. Don't make the face.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I'm trying not to grin. It's not going well.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Yeah. I noticed.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She offers him the ball. When he takes it, she keeps her fingers against his for a brief moment, then lets go with a flushed, annoyed glance at herself.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: We could get lunch on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Actual lunch. Big plates. If somebody serves one leaf and calls it a concept, we're leaving.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I have learned at least one thing about you.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Hopefully more than one.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: She takes the ball back and bounces it once, collecting herself. Her smile returns before she can hide it.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Boku... I'm fine on my own. Always was. You get that, yeah?

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Good. I want you here anyway.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: The coach calls for the last ball. They return it together, then walk toward the gate with time left to spare.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: I don't need to find a weakness that makes her stay. She's beside me because she wants to be, and she's finally said it plainly enough that even I can't miss it.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Svea / Good. Credits, then title.

endings.title: Same Side of the Court
endings.cgBrief: Svea and a charcoal MC silhouette exchange a relaxed friendly fist bump at the hardcourt boundary; sports bag between them, normal daylight, comfortable friendship without romantic framing.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: I like you, Takahashi. Just... not like that. Took a while to be sure. Don't want to keep you guessing now I am.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: All right.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: You can look disappointed. I'm not going to tell you how to take it.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: That blunt permission is unexpectedly useful. I let out the breath I've been holding.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I am disappointed. I still like being around you.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Then take the time you need. Court isn't going anywhere.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Several school days later, the MC joins a supervised casual game. Svea passes him the ball at an entirely reasonable speed and looks surprised when he catches it cleanly.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Training paid off.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: One catch. Don't give a speech.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Afterwards, she offers a fist bump. He returns it.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: Nothing secret is being promised. I don't have to pretend I never wanted more, but I can enjoy being on the same side of the court without treating the game as another chance to win her over.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Lunch?

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Actual lunch?

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Good. You remember.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Svea / Neutral. Credits, then title.

endings.title: The Next Practice
endings.cgBrief: Svea leaves the quiet hardcourt with a basketball under her arm, looking forward; an empty bench behind her, cool natural late light, steady resolved expression. She remains strong and self-directed.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: No. I don't want to date you. I'd rather we stop meeting like this for a while.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I didn't think things were that bad.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: I kept telling you when something bothered me. Too often, you treated it like I was putting on an act you had to get past.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: She shifts the ball under her arm and waits. There isn't a hidden smile underneath the answer.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I understand. I'll give you space.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Good.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She returns the ball to the coach and collects her bag. The MC stays by the bench while she walks toward the building.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: I had wanted to be the person who saw some secret softer version of her. She was showing me who she was all along: hungry after practice, bad at lying, kind to animals, tired some days, interested in her own life.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Good luck at the next practice.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Thanks. Take care, Takahashi.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She leaves. He doesn't call after her or turn her refusal into one last challenge.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: Tomorrow she'll still have a court, a team and things she wants to do. I need to learn how to care about somebody without making myself the reason for all of them.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Svea / Bad. Credits, then title.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: That came out like I wanted to take over. I don't. I'm sorry. I'll stop explaining and hear your answer.

lines.speaker: Svea
lines.text: Good. One terrible sentence doesn't erase everything else. Doesn't get a free pass either. Listen.
